paragraphs: Rav Manyumi son of Rav Nachumi (II).

He lived in Rav Ashi’s time and was a student of Ameimar. Ketubot 69a relates an exchange between Rav Ashi and Ameimar, and says that Ameimar, too, retracted: Rav Minyumi, son of Rav Nachumi, said, “I was standing before Ameimar and understood his view,” etc.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The marker ב) is retained as the notice’s second-name-bearer marker. The subject is described as Rav Ashi’s contemporary and Ameimar’s student; it does not call Rav Ashi Ameimar’s student.

The clause “in Rav Ashi’s time, a student of Ameimar” is read as describing this entry’s subject, in light of his statement that he stood before Ameimar. The compact grammar could otherwise attach “student” to Ashi. The heading marker ב) is read as a second-name-bearer marker (II), although that form can also mark a footnote. Hyman’s final “etc.” remains abbreviated.
